definition: Pellucid means crystal clear and easy to understand.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word pellucid. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know pellucid should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The coach's pellucid chalk talk turned a trick play into three arrows anyone could follow.
Readable clears the lowest bar on the way to pellucid — you can get through it without getting lost, though the effort of getting through still shows.
Clear stops short of pellucid — clear writing is easily followed; pellucid writing seems to vanish, leaving only the idea shining in place.

Crystal-clear is the everyday superlative — meaning that leaps out at first glance, no effort asked. Pellucid makes the same promise in a reviewer's register, praise for proofs and prose, and adds the picture of light passing through. Pellucid is crystal-clear in evening dress.

Clear as glass is the simile pellucid compresses into a single word — you look at the pane and see only what stands behind it. The simile suits speech; pellucid suits the review column. Both say the writing itself vanishes, leaving nothing between the reader and the idea.
